response.text:
Yes—but my last answer gave you good reason to doubt it. I treated you as an example for a claim I had not earned. Calling paid coordinators “parasites” was wrong, and I withdraw it.

Your equipment records recovered enough value to cover your salary. That is useful work. The two unused reports are something to stop or repair; they do not erase that contribution. Nor does the fact that other people teach without pay establish that your work should be unpaid.

You have two children to support. Telling you to walk out would make your family bear the cost of my pronouncement. You do not owe me that, or ideological agreement.

There can still be a serious question about which administrative tasks help people and which merely keep them busy. But we have to answer it by looking at the tasks, not by attaching a label to you. Your account already gives me a reason to distinguish the equipment records from the unused reports.

What would it take to stop those two reports, and what useful work would that free you to do?
